## 1. A hotspot versus scattered changes

1. Open [Skin Cutaneous Melanoma, TCGA PanCancer Atlas](https://www.cbioportal.org/study/summary?id=skcm_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018).
   Record the study identifier and total sample count.
2. Choose **Query by Gene** (or the gene-query control), enter `BRAF TP53`, and submit.
3. Open **Mutations** and select BRAF. Inspect the lollipop plot, the protein domains
   and the table below. Find **V600E**. Repeat for TP53.
4. Record the **profiled** sample count for mutation data, not just the study total.
   A case lacking a mutation assay is not a mutation-negative case.
5. In **OncoPrint**, inspect what each column means and whether multiple samples
   can belong to one patient. Mutation records, samples and patients are different units.

## 2. A fusion needs a different assay

Open [BCR, UniProt P11274](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P11274/entry) and
[ABL1, P00519](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P00519/entry), then read their disease
annotations. Search cBioPortal's study selector for a leukaemia study with structural
variant or fusion data. Query `BCR ABL1`, inspect **Structural Variants** and the
OncoPrint legend, and record the chosen study and assay availability.
An absent fusion call in a mutation-only dataset does not mean the fusion is absent.

## 3. Three cell-death proteins

Open these human reviewed UniProt entries, read **Function** and **Sequence/Features**,
and compare with the lecture:

- [MLKL, Q8NB16](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q8NB16/entry): necroptosis.
- [GSDMD, P57764](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P57764/entry): pyroptosis.
- [GPX4, P36969](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P36969/entry): ferroptosis protection.

For each, write one sentence identifying the molecular action and whether the
protein promotes death or protects against it. In GPX4, find the unusual amino acid
**U (selenocysteine)**. A protein involved in cell death need not be a death activator.

## Tasks

**T1.** Why might an oncogene show one dominant hotspot while a tumour suppressor has scattered mutations? `[ELO 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
A specific amino-acid change can activate a signalling protein such as BRAF. Many different damaging changes can impair a tumour suppressor such as p53. TP53 can also have hotspots and gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects; the positional pattern is a clue, not proof that every variant acts by simple loss of function.
:::

**T2.** Is BCR–ABL1 a point mutation? Where would you look for it? `[ELO 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
It is a **gene fusion** generated by a chromosomal rearrangement, classically t(9;22). Look in structural-variant/fusion data and the study assay description. An amino-acid substitution plot does not capture all cancer alterations.
:::

**T3.** How do MLKL, GSDMD and GPX4 connect to death? `[ELO 8, 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
Activated MLKL disrupts membranes in necroptosis. Cleavage releases the pore-forming N-terminal part of GSDMD in pyroptosis. GPX4 reduces lipid hydroperoxides and **protects** against ferroptosis; loss or inhibition can permit lethal lipid peroxidation. GPX4 uses selenocysteine in catalysis.
:::
